problem: "Purity ranges from 0 to 1" is loose: with non-empty clusters purity can never fall to 0. It is bounded below by 1/(number of gold classes), because every cluster contributes at least its largest class share. Students may state 0 as the minimum in an exam.
fix: Purity ranges from 0 to 1 in principle, but with J gold classes the lowest achievable value is 1/J; it equals 1 when every cluster contains only one gold class. Report k alongside it because purity rises with k.

problem: The graph is declared directed ('directed': True) and the edges run centroid → document. Cluster membership has no direction; drawn as arrows it suggests the centroid 'points to' or 'produces' the document, which can confuse students about what the edges mean.
fix: Mark the graph undirected ('directed': false) and keep the dashed edges as plain membership links between each centroid and its assigned documents.
